beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. Lost {troop_count} men on that flank, a fair price for a lesson I should have remembered.
Ser {player}, you took those {troop_count} men fairly. Come by the fen crossing and I will show you the sinkholes.
You have a sharp eye, {player}, but you pressed the left flank too soon. I will remember that for next time.
{player} has caught me again, and I will not pretend the ditch was not my own fault. Well played, though. We will meet again.

beat_by_player.text: I lost {troop_count} men to {player} today and I am glad of it. Good order, good nerve. The server is better for players like that.
Ser {player}, {troop_count} men went down on that field. Hold that line well and you will do fine against the rest of us.
Your flank was a fine piece of work, {player}. My {troop_count} men will recover, and so will my pride, in time. Bring your best next time.
{player} won that field fair enough, but I will not forget how the rear guard broke. Expect me at the next crossing, with spades.

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work beside {player} against {enemy_faction}. Our {troop_count} held the road, and the new players should study that fight.
Ser {player}, your timing at the ford was excellent. Stay close to my line and we both come home with fewer scars.
We held together well, {player}. {enemy_faction} did not expect {troop_count} men to hold that hill, and neither did I, if I am honest. Shall we do it again?
The old veterans would have lost half those men. {player} and I kept {troop_count} alive against {enemy_faction}.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you let me walk instead of asking for gold. I will return the courtesy when the roads are quieter.
{player} released me without ransom. That is a generous choice, and this server needs more of them.
{player} let me go without ransom. I still will not forgive that ditch, but I thank you for the courtesy.
Ser {player}, your mercy is noted. A debt paid in kindness is harder to forget than gold, and I will remember it.

player_joined_my_faction.text: Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Ask me about the crossings and the old roads, and I will tell you what I can.
Ser {player}, I am glad to have you with {my_faction}. Listen more than you speak in the early skirmishes. That is how I learned.
{player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Let us see what the new blood can do. The good recruits always listened first.
Ser {player}, {my_faction} takes you on, though I want to see your oath proven before I believe it. Prove yourself where it counts.

player_granted_fief.text: {player} has been given {fief}. A fine choice. I hope the walls hold better than mine did in the second siege.
Ser {player}, {fief} is a heavy gift. Walls do not hold themselves, and I have seen good men lose towns to a dry well.
So {player} gets {fief}. I held the fen crossing since the first war with spades alone, and nobody wrote me a song. Good luck.
Ser {player}, I am proud to see {fief} in good hands. If you need advice on drainage or weak ground, you know where to find me.

encounter_greeting.text: Good day, {player}. This is {persona} of {my_faction}. Mind the fen road ahead, the ground is soft and it has swallowed better horses than yours.
Good day, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here. I have walked this road since before your banners were stitched, so I will keep my eyes open.
{player}, {persona} of {my_faction}. I would rather not spend a morning on you, but I will if I must. Stand aside and we may both keep our men.
{player}! {persona} of {my_faction} again. It is good to see a familiar banner out here. How are the roads treating you these days?

encounter_farewell.text: Safe travels, {player}. May the fen mud stay out of your boots and the sinkholes stay where you can see them.
We will part here, {player}. The northern ford is shallower than the map says, and I would not trust the bridge at dusk.
Go on then, {player}. Our paths will cross again, and when they do I expect the same firm handshake you gave my scouts. Good day.
Until the next crossing, {player}. Take a little care on the wet road, and do not let a bit of mud spoil a good ride.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the fen again. Every spring some young rider tries the road to {town} and learns the hard way it is not a road at all.
Has anyone seen the herders from {village} this morning? Their flock was grazing near the ditch and I would hate to see a sheep go in.
Grain in {town} is climbing again. Buy what you can carry now, because the next dry spell will hit the stalls before the carts do.
I have been asked again about the tunnel under the old walls. No, I will not give directions, but the mortar was soft that year.
Good sunrise over the marsh this morning. A man could forget the wars for an hour if he did not know what the mud was hiding.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men on the causeway today. Regroup and come back. The mud forgives everyone eventually.
Ser {player}, I saw what happened to your {troop_count} men. I lost two armies in the first war and still came back. You will too.
A bad day for {player}, with {troop_count} lost. The rest of us have had them, so do not let the loud ones tell you otherwise.
Ser {player}, {troop_count} men gone is a poor showing. Look hard at where your line broke before you march out again.
